text:
anna-support: customer on private VPC reporting intermittent decrypt failures with our KMS proxy. Errors show up as `hsm: handshake failed: tls: unexpected message` and app-level 502s. Happening ~2-3x/hour for them.

mike-sre: can you paste a short timeline/log snippet? is this correlated with deploys? any network changes on their side?

anna-support: timeline: started yesterday 09:40 UTC, recurred every ~20-40m. customer ran `curl` -> got TLS handshake errors intermittently. They say nothing changed in their firewall recently. No deploys on our side during window (checked).

anna-support: paste from their connector logs:
```
2026-10-11T09:40:22Z WARN connector: ksm call failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport: connection is closing
2026-10-11T09:40:22Z ERROR hsm-client: handshake error: tls: unexpected message
2026-10-11T09:40:22Z INFO metrics: request_id=abc123 status=502
```

samir-devex: intermittent TLS unexpected message usually looks like a mid-stream reset or a man-in-the-middle TLS proxy doing something with connection reuse. Ask customer to run `openssl s_client -connect hsm.private.svc:2376 -servername hsm.private.svc -alpn http/1.1` while reproducing. Also check for transparent TLS proxies.

julia-ml: vendor HSM docs mention persistent session multiplexing and that the HSM's management plane uses dynamic ephemeral ports for out-of-band callbacks. Could be NAT/ephemeral port exhaustion or blocked ephemeral port ranges on their egress allowlist.

ben-infra: notes from infra: our private KMS connector expects long-lived TCP connections and uses client certs. If an intermediate proxy or firewall performs TLS interception (breaks client certs) it will cause handshake issues on renegotiation or when ALPN/HTTP2 is negotiated.

kyle-support: customer says they run a managed firewall that only allows outbound 443 and a TCP proxy on port 3128. They do not allow wide ephemeral ranges. Could that cause closures mid-session?

mike-sre: yes — if the KMS client opens both an outgoing TLS session and expects the HSM to connect back (callback) on ephemeral ports, or if NAT translations time out, we can see `transport: connection is closing` then `unexpected message`. Two action items for repro: 1) run `openssl s_client` against the HSM endpoint while reproducing to capture the TLS handshake result, 2) run `tcpdump -w /tmp/hsm.pcap host <hsm-ip> and port 2376` during an incident window.

anna-support: sent repro steps to customer with commands. they returned this output for `openssl`:
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
1400...: TLS handshake complete
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.3
    Cipher    : TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
    Verify return code: 0 (ok)
---
write: error: Broken pipe
```

samir-devex: `Broken pipe` right after TLS session indicates peer closed connection after handshake or mid-session. That could be due to proxy idle timeouts or active TLS interception rejecting client cert on renegotiation. Do they have a corporate proxy doing TLS MITM (squid/bluecoat) configured?

kyle-support: customer confirmed a transparent proxy on egress that re-signs certs. They think it's only for HTTP, but it might be touching TLS traffic on long-lived connections.

julia-ml: vendor HSM client uses TLS session resumption and expects raw client certs. TLS MITM will break that. Also ephemeral port constraints can break callbacks. Ask customer to allow direct egress to HSM IP/port without TLS interception, or whitelist our connector IPs, and open ephemeral port range 32768-61000 for return traffic.

ben-infra: also ask customer to check for TCP RSTs from their firewall around those timestamps. Command for customer: `sudo tcpdump -n -i any 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-rst) != 0 and host <hsm-ip>'`

anna-support: pinged customer with checklist:
- capture pcap during failure (we can analyze)
- run `openssl s_client` and include `-status -showcerts` output
- temporarily bypass TLS/HTTP proxy for the connector to verify whether MITM is root cause
- allow ephemeral port range 32768-61000 for return traffic and confirm NAT timeouts > 1h

hsm-bot: note: recent hsm firmware v2.14 changed session resumption behavior (2026-09-01). Known to fail when a man-in-the-middle terminates client certs.

mike-sre: I'll join the debug call tomorrow 14:00 UTC. If customer can provide pcap and `ss -tnp` showing ESTAB sessions, we can look at whether there are mid-stream FIN/RST or repeated rehandshakes. Also check if their proxy is closing idle connections after 60s.

samir-devex: internal mitigation we can offer: configure connector to reestablish quickly on TLS errors with exponential backoff, add more robust retry semantics and surface a clearer error so the app gets 5xx->retry hint. For Private customers we can also provide guidance to white-list our SANs and avoid TLS interception for the connector certs.

anna-support: customer agreed to run captures and temporarily bypass proxy during maintenance window. Owner: anna-support. Escalated to eng-infra (ben-infra) and devex (samir-devex). Next update expected 2026-10-12 14:30 UTC. :thumbsup:
